text.p: The Dutch government, in its role as president of the European Union, welcomed on Tuesday the accord signed between Germany and the Czech Republic.

"The signature marks a decisive and historic step in the process of good-neighbourly relations and partnership between a EU member state and an associated partner," it said in a brief statement released in the Hague.
"The Presidency would like to express its confidence that the cooperation as envisaged in the Joint German-Czech Declaration will lead to deeper understanding between the two neighbouring peoples."
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus met in Prague to sign the declaration meant to cement post-war reconciliation between the two countries.

In the accord, Bonn expresses its sorrow at the 1938-45 Nazi occupation of Czech lands and Prague its regret at the post-war expulsion of some 2.5 million Sudeten Germans. Germany also backs Czech membership of the European Union and NATO.
